finding: band-limiting the excitation breaks this fitter, and full-band excitation cannot reach enough signal-to-noise on this input chain. That is the impasse.
why: with the excitation confined to 200-2000 Hz the design matrix carries no information above 2 kHz, so the least-squares solution is unconstrained there and the taps run away. The fitter only has a trace*1e-9 ridge, which cannot regularise a rank-deficient band. This is a property of the estimator plus excitation, not of the room.
what_this_means: The one PASS was produced by full-band white noise at the only level the chain can deliver without clipping, and that level leaves only about 6.5 dB of excitation-to-noise.
Raising the SNR requires band-limiting, which in turn makes the estimator ill-conditioned, so L1 explodes and the rejection gate (correctly) refuses the model.
The impasse is therefore structural: full-band is required for conditioning, and full-band at usable SNR is not available from this input chain.

routes_left.hardware: lower the input floor (gain stage, shielded cabling, away from switching supplies). This is the only route that helps both constraints at once.
routes_left.estimator: ask B for a regulariser that matches the excitation bandwidth (ridge scaled to the band, or fit only in the excited band). That would let band-limited excitation be used, which is the only way to raise SNR without clipping.
routes_left.neither: accept the single PASS as the achievable state and report the capability as unproven at this hardware.

status: flow complete and verified; capability still single-instance and not reproducible.
